notes:
v2.6.4 was tagged but never released: the release workflow rejected wp-cli-cf7.php. 2.6.5 is the same release with that check fixed.

Contact form submissions are kept in the site itself now. Every Contact Form
7 message is stored and listed under Kickstarter Settings > CF7 Entries, a
form can send the visitor to a thank-you page after a successful send, and
the release notes on the Updates screen read as formatted text.

### For site administrators
- **Kickstarter Settings > CF7 Entries** lists every Contact Form 7
  message whose mail was sent or failed, newest first, with a count of the
  ones nobody has opened yet. Filter by form, status, dates or a search;
  open one to see every field; mark messages read or delete them, one at a
  time or in bulk; export one form's messages as a CSV file for Excel.
- **A message whose mail failed is marked "Mail failed" in red.** The
  site could not send it, so the entry is the only copy of what the visitor
  wrote: answer from there, and have the site's mail (SMTP) settings
  checked. Tools > Site Health reports failed mails of the last 7 days.
- **"Delete entries older than N days"** on the same screen removes old
  messages once a day, failed mails included. 0, the default, keeps them.
- **Tools > Export Personal Data and Erase Personal Data** include these
  messages: an export lists every message sent with that email address,
  and an erasure deletes those messages whole.
- **A form can send the visitor on after a successful send.** In the form
  editor (Contact > Contact Forms), the new Redirect tab chooses nowhere, a
  page of the site, or an address. An address that is not a web address or
  a path on this site is refused with a notice.
- Uploaded files, IP addresses and browser details are not stored unless
  the developers switch that on.
- The release notes on this screen use the full width, with headings,
  lists and code shown as such.

### Added
- CF7 Entries (`app/Core/Forms/`, `Cf7EntriesAdminPage`, `views/admin/cf7-entries.twig`
  and `cf7-entry.twig`; `docs/forms.md`). Every submission CF7 sends
  (`wpcf7_mail_sent`, status `new`) or fails to send (`wpcf7_mail_failed`,
  status `mail_failed`) goes to `{prefix}codehills_cf7_entries`: form id
  and title, `created_at` in UTC, status, `read_at`, the fields as JSON
  without CF7's own underscore fields, the files, the page it was sent
  from, and a hash that stops a second insert of one submission in one
  request. Spam and aborted sends never reach those hooks. What CF7 says
  must not be stored is not, as Flamingo does: demo mode, `do_not_store`
  or an unchecked `consent_for:storage`, do-not-store tags. The table is
  created with `dbDelta()` on the theme's version change and on the first
  CF7 init, and survives deactivation.
- `wp codehills cf7 drop-table [--yes]`: drops the table and deletes the
  kept files (`app/Console/wp-cli-cf7.php`).
- Filters: `codehills_cf7_entries_capability` (default `manage_options`;
  the retention setting always needs `manage_options`),
  `codehills_cf7_store_ip` (default false: no IP address or user agent),
  `codehills_cf7_store_files` (default false: the entry keeps the file
  names and says the files were not kept).
- Kept files are copied after the insert to
  `uploads/codehills-cf7-files-<suffix>/<entry id>/`, the suffix random
  and stored in `codehills_cf7_files_suffix`, with Apache deny rules and an
  `index.php`, served only through `admin-post.php?action=codehills_cf7_download`
  (capability and a nonce), and deleted with their entry. A failed copy
  keeps the entry and records why.
- Retention: `codehills_cf7_entries_retention_days` and the daily
  `codehills_cf7_entries_retention` event, scheduled only while it is
  above 0 and removed on deactivation.
- A personal data exporter and eraser through the
  `wp_privacy_personal_data_exporters` / `_erasers` filters, matching an
  address as a whole field value.
- CSV export of one form: UTF-8 with a BOM, the date, status and page,
  one column per field, the files. A cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`,
  `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading single quote.
- Delete, bulk delete, export, the retention setting and the eraser go
  through `codehills_kickstarter_log_security_event()`
  (`CF7_ENTRY_DELETED`, `CF7_ENTRIES_BULK_DELETED`,
  `CF7_ENTRIES_EXPORTED`, `CF7_ENTRIES_RETENTION_CHANGED`,
  `CF7_ENTRIES_ERASED`).
- The Site Health test `codehills_cf7_failed_mail`: critical while a mail
  failed in the last 7 days.
- The Redirect tab (`Cf7Redirect`, `views/admin/cf7-redirect-panel.twig`):
  nowhere, a page, or an http(s) URL or same-site path, stored as the
  form's `_codehills_cf7_redirect` meta. The form carries the target in
  `data-codehills-redirect`; `src/js/cf7-redirect.js` follows it on CF7's
  `wpcf7mailsent` event, only to an http(s) URL or a same-origin path. No
  inline script. The Form block renders its shortcode after the block
  cache, so a cached block's form gets its current target.
- `ReleaseNotes::parse()` and `views/admin/partials/release-notes.twig`:
  the Updates screen renders the notes as headings, paragraphs and lists
  with their wrapped lines joined, inline code, bold and fenced code, all
  escaped by Twig; links stay text.
- `views/admin/partials/ui.twig`: the `badge` and `field_class` macros.
- `docs/forms.md`; `tests/js/cf7-redirect.test.mjs` runs in
  `npm run test:admin-js`.

### Changed
- `docs/deploy.md`, "After the site is on the new host", the SMTP item:
  each form's entry appears in CF7 Entries with status New, not in
  Flamingo; Mail failed means fixing SMTP before launch.
- The front-end bundle (`resources/js/tailwind-interactions.js`) carries
  the redirect module; so do the child template's
  `resources/js/site-interactions.js` and the fixture child's build.

### Removed
- Theme Plugins no longer offers WP Migrate Lite or Ultimate Addons for
  Contact Form 7. The theme never uninstalls a plugin: a site that has
  them keeps them.

### Fixed
- The release workflow's production ZIP check rejected a WP-CLI command
  whose name has a digit (`app/Console/wp-cli-cf7.php`), which stopped
  v2.6.4 after its tag. The ZIP was right; the check, inline shell in
  `release.yml` that no job ran before a tag, allowed only
  `wp-cli-[a-z-]+.php`. The checks are now `scripts/release-verify.mjs`
  (`npm run release:verify -- <zip>`, rule `wp-cli-[a-z0-9-]+.php`): the
  release runs it on its ZIP, and the Tests workflow's Production build
  job on the ZIP it builds on every push. `npm run test:release-verify`
  (production-shaped ZIPs: `wp-cli-cf7.php` passes, `create-block.php`
  fails) runs in the Node job.

### Upgrade notes
- **Sites that have Ultimate Addons for Contact Form 7 keep it**, and the
  entries it stored stay there. Turn off its database add-on, or every
  submission is stored twice. A site that uses its other features
  (conditional fields, multistep, columns) keeps the plugin.
- **A redirect set in UACF7 is set again** in the form's Redirect tab
  before UACF7 goes: the theme does not read UACF7's settings.
- **On an existing child site the redirect works only after the child's
  JavaScript is rebuilt**: the child's `resources/js/site-interactions.js`
  replaces the parent's bundle. `wpdev update` or `npm run parent:adopt`
  rebuild it; by hand, run `npm run build:prod` in the child and deploy.
- **CF7 Entries starts empty.** Nothing is imported from UACF7 or
  Flamingo. The screen needs `manage_options` (filter
  `codehills_cf7_entries_capability`); the retention setting always needs
  `manage_options`.
- **Uploaded files are not kept** unless `codehills_cf7_store_files`
  returns true. On Nginx the deny rules are not read, and the random
  folder name is the only protection (`docs/forms.md`). The IP address and
  user agent are stored only with `codehills_cf7_store_ip`.
- **WP Migrate Lite can be deleted**: `wpdev pull`, `npm run pack:site`
  and the Cloudways migrator cover what it did.
